summary: Almost anyone may shecht an animal, and the shechitah is kosher. A non-Jew's shechitah makes the animal a neveilah, but shechting at night, by a blind person, or even on Shabbos, is still kosher.

chunks.en: Everyone may shecht, and their shechitah is kosher,
chunks.st: Everyone slaughters an animal, i.e., can perform halakhically valid slaughter, and their slaughter is valid,

words.note: Shechitah is the kosher way of slaughtering an animal.

chunks.en: except for a deaf-mute,
chunks.st: except for a deaf-mute,

words.note: Someone who cannot hear or speak; the halachah treats him as not responsible.

chunks.en: someone who is not mentally fit, and a child,
chunks.st: an imbecile, and a minor,

chunks.en: because they might ruin their shechitah.
chunks.st: lest they ruin their slaughter because they lack competence.

chunks.en: But if any of them shechted and others watched them,
chunks.st: And for all of them, when they slaughtered an animal and others see and supervise

chunks.en: their shechitah is kosher.
chunks.st: them, their slaughter is valid.

chunks.en: The shechitah of a non-Jew
chunks.st: Slaughter performed by a gentile renders the animal

chunks.en: makes it a neveilah, and it makes a person tamei by carrying it.
chunks.st: an unslaughtered carcass, and the carcass imparts ritual impurity through carrying.

words.note: An animal that died without a kosher shechitah.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts at night,
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters an animal at night,

chunks.en: and also a blind person who shechted,
chunks.st: and likewise in the case of the blind person who slaughters an animal,

chunks.en: his shechitah is kosher.
chunks.st: his slaughter is valid.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts on Shabbos
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters an animal on Shabbat

chunks.en: or on Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: or on Yom Kippur,

chunks.en: even though he deserves the death penalty for it,
chunks.st: although he is liable to receive the death penalty,

chunks.en: his shechitah is kosher.
chunks.st: his slaughter is valid.

summary: You may shecht with a smooth sickle, a sharp stone or a reed. You may not shecht with a saw, teeth or a fingernail, because they choke the animal instead of cutting.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts with a hand sickle,
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters an animal with the smooth side of a hand sickle, which has both a smooth and a serrated side,

chunks.en: with a sharp stone, or with a reed,
chunks.st: or with a sharpened flint, or with a reed that was cut lengthwise and sharpened,

chunks.en: his shechitah is kosher.
chunks.st: his slaughter is valid.

chunks.en: Anyone may shecht, and at any time one may shecht,
chunks.st: All slaughter [hakkol shoḥatin], and one may always slaughter,

chunks.en: and one may shecht with anything,
chunks.st: and one may slaughter with any item that cuts,

chunks.en: except for a harvest sickle,
chunks.explain: It has teeth, like a saw.
chunks.st: except for the serrated side of the harvest sickle,

chunks.en: a saw, and teeth,
chunks.st: a saw, the teeth of an animal when attached to its jawbone,

chunks.en: and a fingernail, because they choke the animal.
chunks.st: and a fingernail, because they are serrated and they consequently strangle the animal and do not cut its windpipe and gullet as required.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts with a harvest sickle, moving it forward,
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters an animal with a harvest sickle, which is serrated with its teeth inclined considerably in one direction, in a forward direction, where the serrations do not tear the flesh,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is pasul,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai deem the slaughter not valid

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is kosher.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel deem it valid.

chunks.en: And if its teeth were smoothed down,
chunks.st: And they both agree that if they smoothed its serrations so that they do not tear the flesh, its halakhic status

chunks.en: it is just like a knife.
chunks.st: is like that of a knife and one may slaughter with it.

summary: The shechitah cut belongs below the ring at the top of the windpipe. If he cut inside the ring but left a thin line of it whole, it is still kosher.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts inside the ring and left of it
chunks.explain: The ring is the hard ring at the top of the windpipe.
chunks.st: With regard to one who slaughters an animal from within the cricoid cartilage that forms a complete ring at the top of the windpipe

chunks.en: a thread's width all around it,
chunks.st: and left a thread breadth over the surface of the ring in its entirety intact, as the knife did not go beyond the ring toward the head of the animal,

chunks.en: his shechitah is kosher.
chunks.st: his slaughter is valid.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei the son of Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

chunks.en: even a thread's width over most of it is enough.
chunks.st: It is valid even if he left a thread breadth over the majority of the surface of the ring.

summary: Shechitah is done from the front of the neck, but melikah (the way a Kohen kills a bird korban with his fingernail) is done from the back of the neck. What is right for one is wrong for the other.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts from the sides, his shechitah is kosher.
chunks.st: One who slaughters from the sides of the throat, his slaughter is valid.

chunks.en: Someone who does melikah from the sides,
chunks.explain: Melikah: the Kohen cuts a bird korban's neck with his fingernail.
chunks.st: One who pinches the neck of a bird offering from the sides,

chunks.en: his melikah is pasul.
chunks.st: his pinching is not valid.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts from the back of the neck,
chunks.st: One who slaughters from the nape [oref] of the neck,

chunks.en: his shechitah is pasul.
chunks.st: his slaughter is not valid.

chunks.en: Someone who does melikah from the back of the neck,
chunks.st: One who pinches a bird offering from the nape of the neck,

chunks.en: his melikah is kosher.
chunks.st: his pinching is valid.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts from the front of the neck,
chunks.st: One who slaughters from the throat,

chunks.en: his shechitah is kosher.
chunks.st: his slaughter is valid.

chunks.en: Someone who does melikah from the front of the neck,
chunks.st: One who pinches a bird offering from the throat,

chunks.en: his melikah is pasul,
chunks.st: his pinching is not valid,

chunks.en: because the whole back of the neck is right for melikah,
chunks.st: as the entire nape is valid for pinching

chunks.en: and the whole front of the neck is right for shechitah.
chunks.st: and the entire throat is valid for slaughter.

chunks.en: So we find: what is kosher for shechitah
chunks.st: It is found that that which is valid for slaughter is

chunks.en: is pasul for melikah,
chunks.st: not

chunks.en: and what is kosher for melikah
chunks.st: valid for pinching and that which is valid for pinching is

chunks.en: is pasul for shechitah.
chunks.st: not valid for slaughter.

summary: Bird korbanos can be turtledoves (grown birds) or young pigeons. The age that is right for one kind is wrong for the other, and when the feathers start turning yellow, the bird is not right for either.

chunks.en: What is kosher in turtledoves
chunks.st: The age that is fit for sacrifice in doves, mature birds, is

chunks.en: is pasul in young pigeons.
chunks.explain: Young pigeons must still be young.
chunks.st: unfit for sacrifice in pigeons, immature birds;

chunks.en: What is kosher in young pigeons
chunks.st: the age that is fit for sacrifice in pigeons

chunks.en: is pasul in turtledoves.
chunks.st: is unfit for sacrifice in doves.

chunks.en: When the feathers start to turn yellow,
chunks.st: At the intermediate stage of the beginning of the yellowing of its plumage (see 22b),

chunks.en: the bird is pasul for both kinds.
chunks.st: a bird is unfit both as this, a pigeon, and as that, a dove, since it is no longer a fledgling but is not yet a mature bird.

stIntro: It is written with regard to bird offerings: “He shall bring his offering of doves, or of young pigeons” (Leviticus 1:14).

summary: The mishnah lists more pairs where something that is right in one case is wrong in another: two kinds of special cows, Kohanim and Levi'im, different kinds of vessels, and bitter and sweet almonds.

chunks.en: What is kosher in the parah adumah
chunks.explain: The red cow whose ashes make people tahor.
chunks.st: That which is fit in a red heifer

words.note: The parah adumah, the red cow.

chunks.en: is pasul in the eglah arufah.
chunks.explain: The calf brought when a dead person is found and no one knows who killed him.
chunks.st: is unfit in a heifer whose neck is broken;

words.note: The eglah arufah, a young cow.

chunks.en: What is kosher in the eglah arufah
chunks.st: that which is fit in a heifer whose neck is broken

chunks.en: is pasul in the parah adumah.
chunks.st: is unfit in a red heifer.

chunks.en: Something that is fine for Kohanim
chunks.st: There is an element with which priests remain fit and

chunks.en: makes Levi'im pasul.
chunks.st: Levites are unfit,

chunks.en: Something that is fine for Levi'im
chunks.st: and there is also an element with which Levites remain fit and

chunks.en: makes Kohanim pasul.
chunks.st: priests are unfit.

chunks.en: What is tahor in a clay vessel
chunks.st: That which is ritually pure in an earthenware vessel

chunks.en: is tamei in all other vessels.
chunks.st: is ritually impure in all the other types of vessels;

chunks.en: What is tahor in all other vessels
chunks.st: that which is ritually pure in all the other types of vessels

chunks.en: is tamei in a clay vessel.
chunks.st: is ritually impure in an earthenware vessel.

chunks.en: What is tahor in wooden vessels
chunks.st: That which is ritually pure in wooden vessels

chunks.en: is tamei in metal vessels.
chunks.st: is ritually impure in metal vessels;

chunks.en: What is tahor in metal vessels
chunks.st: that which is ritually pure in metal vessels

chunks.en: is tamei in wooden vessels.
chunks.st: is ritually impure in wooden vessels.

chunks.en: The stage of growth when bitter almonds must have ma'aser taken
chunks.explain: Ma'aser is the tenth of the crops that must be given away.
chunks.st: With regard to the obligation of separating teruma and tithes, the stage of development that is obligated in bitter almonds

chunks.en: is when sweet almonds do not need it.
chunks.st: is exempt in sweet almonds;

chunks.en: And when sweet almonds must have ma'aser taken,
chunks.st: and the stage in development that is obligated in sweet almonds

chunks.en: bitter almonds do not need it.
chunks.st: is exempt in bitter almonds.

summary: More pairs: temed (a weak drink made from grape leftovers), brothers who are partners, a girl's father, yibum, and Yom Tov next to Shabbos. Where one rule applies, the other does not.

chunks.en: Temed, before it turned sour,
chunks.explain: Temed is water soaked in leftover grape skins.
chunks.st: Temed, a beverage produced from grape residue soaked in water, until it fermented,

chunks.en: may not be bought with ma'aser money,
chunks.explain: Ma'aser sheni money is spent on food in Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: may not be purchased with second-tithe money to be drunk in Jerusalem, because it is not wine.

chunks.en: and it makes a mikveh pasul.
chunks.st: And if three log of it fall into a ritual bath, its halakhic status is that of drawn water and it invalidates the ritual bath.

chunks.en: Once it fermented, it may be bought with ma'aser money, and it does not
chunks.st: Once it fermented, it is wine, and therefore it may be purchased with second-tithe money and it does not

chunks.en: make a mikveh pasul.
chunks.st: invalidate the ritual bath.

chunks.en: Brothers who are partners,
chunks.st: With regard to brothers who are partners in the inheritance of their father,

chunks.en: when they must add the kalbon,
chunks.explain: A small extra coin added to the half-shekel.
chunks.st: when they are obligated to add the premium [kalbon] to their annual half-shekel payment to the Temple,

chunks.en: do not need to give ma'aser from their animals.
chunks.st: they are exempt from animal tithe;

chunks.en: When they must give ma'aser from their animals,
chunks.st: when they are obligated to separate animal tithe,

chunks.en: they do not need to add the kalbon.
chunks.st: they are exempt from adding the premium.
chunks.stMore: Partners who pay the half-shekel are required to add the premium and are exempt from animal tithe. If they are not true partners, but their inheritance remains the property of the father, the sons are exempt from paying the premium, and they are obligated to separate animal tithe.

chunks.en: Whenever a father may sell his daughter as a maidservant,
chunks.st: Any situation where there is sale of one’s daughter as a Hebrew maidservant, i.e., when she is a minor,

chunks.en: there is no fine.
chunks.explain: A fine the Torah sets that is paid to her father.
chunks.st: there is no fine
chunks.stMore: of fifty sela paid to her father if she is raped or seduced, as that fine is paid to her father only when she is a young woman.

chunks.en: And whenever there is a fine,
chunks.st: And any situation where there is a fine paid to the father

chunks.en: there is no selling.
chunks.st: there is no sale.

chunks.en: Whenever a young girl may use mi'un,
chunks.explain: Mi'un: a young girl married off by her mother or brothers may say no to the marriage.
chunks.st: Any situation where there is the right of refusal for a minor girl married by her mother or brothers, enabling her to opt out of the marriage,

chunks.en: there is no chalitzah.
chunks.explain: Chalitzah frees a widow from marrying her husband's brother.
chunks.st: there is no ḥalitza, as a minor girl whose husband died without children cannot perform ḥalitza.

chunks.en: And whenever there is chalitzah,
chunks.st: And any situation where there is ḥalitza, once she has reached majority,

chunks.en: there is no mi'un.
chunks.st: there is no right of refusal.

chunks.en: Whenever the shofar is blown before Shabbos or Yom Tov,
chunks.st: Any situation where there is a shofar blast sounded on the eve of Shabbat or a Festival to stop the people from performing labor and to demarcate between the sacred and the profane,

chunks.en: there is no Havdalah.
chunks.st: there is no havdala recited at the conclusion of the Shabbat or Festival in prayer and over a cup of wine.

chunks.en: And whenever there is Havdalah,
chunks.st: And any situation where there is havdala recited,

chunks.en: the shofar is not blown.
chunks.st: there is no shofar blast sounded.

chunks.he: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: When Yom Tov falls on Erev Shabbos,
chunks.st: How so? On a Festival that occurs on Shabbat eve,

chunks.en: we blow the shofar, and we do not make Havdalah.
chunks.st: one sounds the shofar to stop the people from performing labor that is permitted on the Festival and prohibited on Shabbat and to demarcate between one sacred day and another; and one does not recite havdala,
chunks.stMore: as that is recited only when the transition is from a sacred day to a profane day or from a day of greater sanctity to a day of lesser sanctity. The sanctity of Shabbat is greater than the sanctity of the Festival, and therefore havdala is not recited in this case.

chunks.en: When Yom Tov falls on Motza'ei Shabbos,
chunks.st: On a Festival that occurs at the conclusion of Shabbat,

chunks.en: we make Havdalah, but we do not blow the shofar.
chunks.st: one recites havdala, but one does not sound the shofar.

chunks.en: How do we make Havdalah then?
chunks.st: How does one recite havdala in that case; i.e., what is the formula of the blessing? It concludes:

chunks.en: "He who separates between holy and holy."
chunks.st: Who distinguishes between sacred and sacred,
chunks.stMore: as opposed to the standard blessing at the conclusion of Shabbat: Who distinguishes between sacred and profane.

chunks.en: Rabbi Dosa says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Dosa says that the formula is: Who distinguishes

chunks.en: "Between very holy and less holy."
chunks.st: between greater sanctity and lesser sanctity.
